habitat.label: Earth reference
habitat.source: NASA Space Apps 2026 challenge brief; Earth sea-level air 14.7 psia / 21% O2 (quiescent)
habitat.line: Earth reference: gravity 9.81 m/s², pressure 14.7 psia, O₂ 21%, vent speed 0 cm/s (assumed), flame size 10 mm (assumed).

verdicts.label: Prevention
verdicts.rule: evidence if M3 (gas flames) and M4 (SAFFIRE solids) are both covered at this habitat; partial if exactly one is; no evidence if neither is.
verdicts.because: M3 (gas flame self-extinction) and M4 (SAFFIRE solid-material burn extent) are covered at this habitat. Transfer confidence is low for M3 and M4 (the engine's own rating of how well the tests carry over to this habitat; see each metric's transfer note).

verdicts.label: Flame behaviour
verdicts.rule: evidence if M1, M2 and M5 are all covered at this habitat; partial if one or two are; no evidence if none is.
verdicts.because: M1 (droplet flame self-extinction), M2 (droplet extinction diameter) and M5 (SPICE coflow flame window) are covered at this habitat. Transfer confidence is low for M1, M2 and M5 (the engine's own rating of how well the tests carry over to this habitat; see each metric's transfer note).

verdicts.label: Detection
verdicts.rule: always partial: smoke sizes were measured (SAME-R) and a simulation compares Earth gravity with microgravity (PSI-115), but there are no lunar dust data and no cited detector size sensitivity, and none of this evidence depends on the habitat's pressure or O2 (ADR-0007).
verdicts.because: Smoke particle sizes from heated spacecraft materials were measured (SAME-R, PSI-101) and one smoke-versus-dust size comparison exists (Arizona Road Dust, DAFT, PSI-47), but there are no lunar dust data and no cited source for which particle sizes detectors respond to. This evidence does not depend on the habitat's pressure or O₂. Only the PSI-115 simulation is about gravity, and its Earth-gravity case matches this habitat.

verdicts.label: Suppression
verdicts.rule: evidence if the R2 dilution curves have covered points (fraction > 0, M1 applicable) for both CO2 and helium; partial if for one of them; no evidence if for neither.
verdicts.because: FLEX dilution tests cover this atmosphere for CO₂ up to 60% (12 of 14 diluted points) and helium up to 45% (14 of 14 diluted points); these show how dilution changed droplet flames in tests, not how an extinguisher performs.

key_numbers.label: P(droplet flame self-extinguishes before burnout)
key_numbers.text: M1 P(droplet flame self-extinguishes before burnout): 93.9% (90% band 59.1% to 99.5%); transfer confidence low.

key_numbers.label: Extinction diameter
key_numbers.text: M2 Extinction diameter: 4 mm (90% band 1.1 mm to 4.67 mm); transfer confidence low.

key_numbers.label: P(gas flame self-extinguishes vs flow-terminated)
key_numbers.text: M3 P(gas flame self-extinguishes vs flow-terminated): 97.2% (90% band 89.5% to 99.7%); transfer confidence low.

key_numbers.label: Solid material burn extent
key_numbers.text: M4 Solid material burn extent: complete burn; transfer confidence low.

key_numbers.label: Supported coflow window
key_numbers.text: M5 Supported coflow window: 96.3% (90% band 4.96% to 97%); transfer confidence low.

drivers.text: About 60% of this band is the gravity honesty widening (ADR-0005): the tests had no buoyancy, and at this gravity and vent speed every plausible flame is at least partly buoyancy-driven. No physics input can remove it; only fire tests run in partial gravity, which the PSI data do not have, could.

About 50% of this band comes from the model itself: 77 PSI-69 tests lie within the honesty-gate distance of this atmosphere. More tests near 21.0% O2 and 14.7 psia would shrink it the most. No Planner candidate is close to this habitat.

About 55% of this band is the gravity honesty widening (ADR-0005): the tests had no buoyancy, and at this gravity and vent speed every plausible flame is at least partly buoyancy-driven. No physics input can remove it; only fire tests run in partial gravity, which the PSI data do not have, could.

gaps.text: No lunar dust or lunar dust simulant data exists in these PSI files. The only dust measured (DAFT) is Arizona Road Dust. So "could lunar dust fool a smoke detector?" is an open question here, not an answered one.
We have no cited source for which particle sizes ionization and light-scattering smoke detectors respond to, so the page does not show detector size ranges.

FLEX tested CO₂ dilution only between 14% and 24% O₂ (0.69-3.05 atm). This habitat (21% O₂, 1.00 atm) is close enough to those tests (distance <= 2, ADR-0006) for CO₂ fractions up to 60%; beyond that there is no evidence and the curve has a gap. Gravity does not change these numbers; it only widens the band (ADR-0005).
gaps.safety_note: CO₂ at these concentrations is dangerous to breathe. Spacecraft use portable CO₂ or water-mist extinguishers aimed at the fire, not cabin flooding. This shows how dilution affected flames in NASA's tests; it is not an operating procedure.

gaps.text: FLEX tested helium dilution only between 13% and 24% O₂ (0.69-1.01 atm). This habitat (21% O₂, 1.00 atm) is close enough to those tests (distance <= 2, ADR-0006) for helium fractions up to 45%. Gravity does not change these numbers; it only widens the band (ADR-0005).
gaps.safety_note: Changing a cabin's gas mix changes what the crew breathes. This shows how helium dilution affected flames in NASA's FLEX tests; it is not an operating procedure or extinguisher guidance.

next_tests.rule: Relevance = the planner's own score x its re-scoring kernel between this habitat and the candidate (atmosphere distance, gravity scale 2 m/s², vent scale 10 cm/s), in place of its three fixed target weights. A dilution candidate is a test at that cabin atmosphere with CO₂ added, so the CO₂ term is left out. Top 3 of the planner's ranked list.

items.rationale: Extinction diameter at Mars gravity (0.378 g), 10.2 psia / 26.5% O2, vent 20 cm/s: the current 90% band is 0.96 wide (relative), 93% of physics samples are in the mixed regime where neither 0 g nor 1 g data apply, and the atmosphere is close to the exploration vehicle 10.2 psia / 26.5% O2 target (weight 0.70).

Extinction diameter at Moon gravity (0.165 g), 10.2 psia / 26.5% O2, vent 10 cm/s: the current 90% band is 1.00 wide (relative), 72% of physics samples are in the mixed regime where neither 0 g nor 1 g data apply, and the atmosphere is close to the exploration vehicle 10.2 psia / 26.5% O2 target (weight 0.70).

Dilution at high O2: P(droplet flame self-extinguishes before burnout) with 20% CO2 replacing nitrogen at Mars gravity (0.378 g), 8.2 psia / 34% O2, vent 20 cm/s. FLEX tested CO2 dilution only at 14-24% O2, so the suppression calculator has no evidence here (honesty gate); 93% of physics samples are in the mixed regime, and the atmosphere is the lunar/Mars base 8.2 psia / 34% O2 target (weight 1.00). A droplet test here tells whether CO2 suppression works the same way in oxygen-enriched cabin air.

next_tests.note: None of the planner's 10 candidates is close to this habitat (kernel distance over 2); these are the closest. The planner targets lunar, Mars, exploration and ISS atmospheres in partial gravity.

history.rule: Closest R1 incident atmosphere by atmosphere distance (O₂ and pressure); shown only within distance 2, the same reach as the honesty gate.
history.text: Artemis II smoke alarm (2026) and Mir oxygen-generator fire (1997) happened at 21% O₂ and 14.7 psia, the same atmosphere as this habitat (the incident's atmosphere is an assumed value, not a recorded one). Gravity there was 0 m/s², here it is 9.81 m/s². The replay shows what today's data say about those conditions; it does not judge what happened.

trust.text: Honesty test (ADR-0009): hiding one tested atmosphere at a time and refitting, the 90% band held for 72 of 74 M1 atmospheres, 58 of 65 M2 atmospheres and 78 of 83 M3 atmospheres under the overlap rule, which is lenient for groups of 1-3 tests. Under the strict rule (observed share inside the band) it held for 7 of 74 (M1) and 4 of 83 (M3). In the wide check (a whole 0.10 O₂ band hidden at once) M3 had only 9 covered groups, a weak test. The test ran in microgravity (0 g), so the gravity widening of partial-gravity bands is not tested by it. M4: the SAFFIRE hindcast scored 7 of 9, the same as a constant rule, so it is not discriminative.

footer.disclaimer: Not an operating procedure. This briefing summarises what NASA's PSI test data can and cannot say about fires in this habitat; it is not a design certification or crew guidance.
